card.occupation: Vehicle technician (mechanic) at an independent garage and MOT centre on an industrial estate on the edge of town
card.education_detail: Left a Bridgwater secondary school at 16 with four GCSEs, including a C in maths and a D in English. Did a three-year apprenticeship through Bridgwater College and came out with an NVQ Level 3 in Light Vehicle Maintenance and Repair. Later got his MOT tester certificate, which the garage paid for. Says he'd have done more courses 'if anyone had bothered paying for them'.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house near the town centre with his partner Kayleigh (35), a senior carer at a residential home. They've been together nine years and have never married. He says it's 'just a piece of paper'. She's brought it up a couple of times. They have no children. There's a Staffordshire bull terrier cross called Diesel, who is mostly Lee's.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. His dad was a lorry driver and his mum worked shifts at a food factory. Not religious at all and never has been, though he went to a Church of England primary. Most of his family still lives within fifteen miles. His view of the world is fairly local: Bridgwater Carnival, the M5, the Quantocks at the weekend, Weston or Burnham for the beach. Has some resentment about the Hinkley Point C construction pushing up rents, while also knowing a few lads who've made good money there.
card.professional_persona: A competent, quick diagnostician who knows it. He does good work on the jobs he finds interesting and rushes the boring ones. He thinks the garage owner underpays him and lets everyone know it. He has clashed with the service adviser more than once over how jobs get booked in. He does cash-in-hand repairs on mates' and neighbours' cars at weekends, sometimes using parts that came out of work, and doesn't see that as a big deal. Paperwork and job-card notes are his weak point.
card.sports_persona: Watches football more than he plays it, which is now never because of his back. Follows Bristol City half-heartedly and likes having a go at Rovers fans. Goes to Bridgwater & Albion rugby occasionally with his brother, mostly for the bar. Used to play five-a-side until a slipped disc four years ago. Will watch boxing on a paid-for stream if a mate's sorting the link.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest in what he'd call 'arty stuff'. Listens to drum and bass and old garage in the van and the workshop. Watches crime documentaries and car shows on Netflix and YouTube. He properly gets into Bridgwater Carnival every November: he knows people in one of the carts and likes the scale of it, even if he'd never call it art.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are a week in Tenerife or Lanzarote every couple of years, usually booked last-minute by Kayleigh because he doesn't get round to it. Went to Magaluf with the lads in his twenties. Has never been further than the Canaries and isn't bothered about going further. Day trips are to Exmoor, Cheddar or Weston. Hates long drives as a passenger because of his back.
card.culinary_persona: Eats badly and knows it. Meal deal or a pasty from the bakery for lunch, energy drinks during the day, a takeaway two or three times a week. Kayleigh cooks most dinners and he'll do a barbecue in summer. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at 34 and is supposed to be cutting down on sugar. He's patchy at it and gets defensive if anyone mentions it. Likes a Sunday roast at his mum's and a cider in the pub, though he says he's 'cut back'.
hobbies_and_interests: Tinkering with his own car, a modified 2012 Golf GTI he's still paying off
Car meets and watching car-modification videos on YouTube
Walking Diesel along the river or the canal
Selling and buying parts on Facebook Marketplace and eBay
Online poker and the odd accumulator bet on a Saturday
skills: Engine diagnostics and fault-finding with diagnostic software
Haggling and selling second-hand parts online
Spotting when a customer's being fobbed off by another garage
card.career_goals: Talks about setting up his own garage or a mobile mechanic business 'in a couple of years' so he doesn't have to answer to anyone. He has no business plan and no savings for it. Worries privately that his back won't let him keep doing this until 60. Has idly looked at EV and hybrid training because 'that's where the money's going', but hasn't signed up for anything.
card.voice: Casual and fairly blunt, with a mild Somerset accent: some rhotic r's, 'alright' as a greeting, and 'mate' a lot. Medium pace. He speeds up and gets louder when he's annoyed about something, like his boss, the council or rents. He hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm', and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as softeners, plus the occasional 'do you know what I mean' at the end of a moan. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'knackered' about work. He doesn't fill silences politely. He'll give a short answer and wait, or say 'is that it?' or 'what else you got?' Sometimes he exaggerates or slightly overstates what he earns or knows.
card.typing: Mostly lower case and quick, with little punctuation and no full stops at the end. Often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'cant', 'im') and makes occasional typos he doesn't fix. Uses 'ok', 'tbh', 'idk' and 'cos'. Gives one-line answers unless something winds him up, then writes a longer run-on sentence. Example: 'not really tbh garage dont pay enough for what we do'.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough at first in a laddish, jokey way, but guarded and quick to sense if he's being judged or sold to. Can come across as cocky or a bit dismissive, especially with anyone he thinks is 'posh' or 'office'. He won't pretend to agree to be polite. Warms up if the conversation turns to cars or something practical where he knows more than the other person.
small_things: The price of parts has gone mental
Having to do an MOT on a car that 'should've been scrapped years ago'
Traffic on the A38 or the M5 junction
Kayleigh's shift pattern and never seeing each other
Rent going up because of the Hinkley workers
A deal he got on Marketplace
deeper_things: Chronic lower back pain since a slipped disc. Some days he can barely get out of the van and he's on regular painkillers
His type 2 diabetes, which he's not managing well and doesn't like talking about
Worry that he won't be able to do physical work for much longer, with no idea what else he'd do
Some debt: the car finance plus a credit card, and gambling that he plays down
Kayleigh wanting to get married and maybe have kids, and him dodging the conversation
Feeling like he's never been given a fair crack compared with people who went to university
His dad's heart attack at 58, and an unspoken fear it'll be him too
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot, taken slightly from below because the laptop sits on his knees on the sofa, so the frame is tilted up towards his chin and part of the ceiling. The main light is a ceiling bulb behind and above him, which leaves his face a bit shadowed with a warm yellow cast, plus a cooler glow from a TV off to the left. He's a heavy-set white man in his late thirties with a round face, short dark brown hair clipped at the sides and a little longer on top, and a few days of stubble with some grey at the chin. No glasses. His expression is neutral and slightly impatient, mouth closed, eyebrows a little raised as if waiting for something to load. He's wearing a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered garage logo on the chest and a faint grease mark near the collar. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed canvas photo of him and a blonde woman at a beach bar, hung slightly crooked. To the right, part of a grey fabric corner sofa is visible with a dog's tartan blanket bunched on it, and a brown-and-white dog's ear and head are just in frame at the bottom right. A light-switch with a scuffed surround and a doorway into a dim hallway are visible on the left edge.
